key_insight: Large vision-language models still struggle at certain kinds of visual reasoning because training captions routinely omit tacit, supervisory details (reporting bias); increasing scale alone does not recover that missing supervision.
problem_solved: Explains why state-of-the-art VLMs fail on fine-grained or compositional visual reasoning by identifying reporting bias in real-world caption data as a core barrier to learning those capabilities.
method: Analyze the text–image training corpora (e.g., data behind OpenCLIP) to quantify how often captions omit concrete visual facts (reporting bias).
Design targeted evaluation/probing tasks that require the tacit information captions typically leave out, and measure model performance across scales.
Compare outcomes and run controlled interventions (e.g., enriched or synthetic captions / targeted supervision) to isolate the effect of reporting bias versus model scale.
impact: Highlights that improving VLM reasoning requires better supervision and dataset design, not just larger models or more data; practitioners should audit caption distributions and add targeted annotations or synthetic descriptions to teach missing facts.
visual_elements: Schematic illustrating reporting bias: an image with a typical caption (high-level) vs. a detailed caption (tacit facts) side-by-side.
Bar/line chart showing reasoning performance plateauing as model/data scale increases, annotated to indicate where missing supervision explains gaps.
Heatmap or histogram of caption content analysis showing frequency of omitted visual facts (e.g., counts, relationships, attributes).
Flow diagram of recommended fixes: dataset audit → targeted annotation/synthesis → retraining/evaluation.
paper_title: Scale Can't Overcome Pragmatics: The Impact of Reporting Bias on Vision-Language Reasoning
paper_authors: Amita Kamath, Jack Hessel, Khyathi Chandu, Jena D. Hwang, Kai-Wei Chang
